familiarity with a dialect is not only reflected by a more efficient processing of familiar dialect words, but also by a more robust processing of dialect words in general.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the N400-effect reflects a semantic processing mechanism that is not affected by dialect-specific differences in pronunciation and vocabulary, while the LPC-effect reflects a control mechanism that is affected by dialect-specific pronunciation differences.
familiarity with dialect words and their pronunciation variants impacts the neural processes of phonology and semantics in children, but in a different way.
dialects, as a form of linguistic variation, are not only a challenge for children’s language development but also a challenge for the brain to process.

familiarity with a dialect is a crucial factor for neural processing of dialect-specific words.
